answer: Coordinated-claim escrow tax. Each identity's first claim must escrow a fee proportional to how many other identities claim in the same window; the fee is refunded only if the cohort's joint claims diverge, so mass-created identities pay escalating shared costs. An attacker forging an ocean of agents pays the full cohort tax on every one, scaling with coordination size. Honest actors claim in small, unaligned groups and pay near zero, a fable of cheap individuality rather than costly crowds. The escrow is held in a shale-like ledger anyone can audit, so duplicate timing patterns expose farms.
